claims.statement: Open-Inspect splits durable state across four Cloudflare primitives: D1 (DB binding) is the single global relational database and authority for every cross-session fact; each SessionDO owns a synchronous per-session SQLite database at ctx.storage.sql; R2 (MEDIA_BUCKET) holds attachment/screenshot/video objects; KV (REPOS_CACHE) holds only short-lived caches and is never a source of truth.

D1 is authoritative for global state and the DO owns live session state: session creation writes the D1 sessions row (plus repository snapshot, skill manifest, and provider-auth snapshot) in one atomic batch before POSTing /internal/init to the DO, and compensates to status 'failed' if DO init fails.

The SqlDatabase port in db/sql-database.ts is a compile-time-only surface: D1Database satisfies it structurally (proven by _AssertExtends<D1Database, SqlDatabase>), so no runtime wrapper exists in production; it deliberately excludes the session DO's synchronous SqlStorage, which has a load-bearing sync contract.

The SqlDatabase port carries three load-bearing contracts: batch() is atomic with positional 1:1 results; meta.changes is required because roughly 38 store call sites gate correctness on it (CAS conflict detection, guarded lifecycle transitions, upsert/insert detection); and statements passed to batch() must originate from the same database's prepare().

instrumentD1 wraps every statement's terminal methods (run/first/all) and batch to record query_ms, d1_server_ms, rows_read, rows_written into a per-request RequestMetrics collector; batch unwraps instrumented statements via the ORIGINAL_STMT symbol because a database can only execute its own prepared statements, and the summary spreads into the http.request wide event as d1_query_count, d1_total_ms, d1_server_total_ms, d1_rows_read, d1_rows_written.

An ESLint rule banning MemberExpression[property.name='DB'] outside composition roots (router, cron entrypoints, queue consumers, SessionDO constructor) enforces that route handlers only reach D1 through ctx.db, so every query is instrumented.

Each D1 store follows a consistent shape: constructor takes SqlDatabase, snake_case rows in the database map to camelCase types at the API boundary; stores include SessionIndexStore, SessionInboxStore, AutomationStore, IntegrationSettingsStore, UserStore, EnvironmentStore, ImageBuildStore, AnalyticsStore, SessionPullRequestStore, the scoped-secrets stores, SkillStore, and the model-provider-account stores.

D1's per-statement bound-parameter ceiling is MAX_D1_QUERY_PARAMETERS = 100; stores must chunk caller-sized IN lists by it (session-list-metadata, skills, skill-profiles) and bulkInsertStatements packs multi-row INSERTs so each statement stays under it, while repo-metadata chunks batch() at 100 statements per call.

The session Durable Object's SQLite schema (session/schema.ts) includes session, participants, messages, events, artifacts, attachments, sandbox, session_repositories, session_diff, session_alarm_state, and ws_client_mapping; initSchema runs SCHEMA_SQL plus the numbered in-code MIGRATIONS plus INDEXES_SQL on every DO activation, and migration entries must be added both to SCHEMA_SQL (fresh DOs) and to MIGRATIONS (existing DOs).

The DO schema enforces 'at most one processing message per session' via the partial unique index idx_messages_one_processing and web-prompt idempotency via idx_messages_client_request_id (both in INDEXES_SQL); message repositories claim work with UPDATE ... RETURNING inside ctx.storage.transactionSync transactions.

D1 migrations are plain SQL files in terraform/d1/migrations named NNNN_description.sql; scripts/d1-migrate.sh validates unique numeric prefixes, creates the _schema_migrations (version, name, applied_at) ledger, and submits each migration with its ledger INSERT in one atomic remote file execution so a committed migration always has its ledger row and is safe to retry.

Integration tests apply the exact production migration files via applyD1Migrations(env.DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS) in test/integration/apply-migrations.ts, wired as the setup file in vitest.integration.config.ts; the pool isolates D1 storage per test file, so within a file tests share one D1 instance and must call cleanD1Tables() (a multi-table DELETE plus skills_catalog_state reset) in beforeEach/afterEach.

Secrets and tokens are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM (auth/crypto.ts: random 96-bit IV prepended to ciphertext, base64 combined) under three distinct keys: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY for SCM tokens (participants.scm_*_encrypted, user_scm_tokens), REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY for global/repo/environment scoped secrets, and PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY for model-provider credentials with associated-data binding preventing replay across accounts.

Secrets-at-rest encryption is fail-closed: env-validation.ts requires TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY and REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY to be strict base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes (rejecting malformed keys and short-key AES downgrades), throws at first touch when absent, and the session runtime enforces both keys at graph build so no path can persist a secret in plaintext.

The scoped-secrets stores share validation (key pattern, MAX_VALUE_SIZE 16 KiB, MAX_TOTAL_VALUE_SIZE 64 KiB per scope, MAX_SECRETS_PER_SCOPE 50, reserved keys) and environment-secret import copies ciphertext verbatim from a member repo because both scopes share one encryption key, so plaintext never transits the control plane.

D1 has no interactive transactions, so ordering safety is achieved with single-statement guards, partial unique indexes, and batch atomicity: guarded UPDATE ... WHERE returning (result.meta?.changes ?? 0) > 0 is the standard CAS idiom across stores (softDelete/pause/resume, advanceNextRunAt strictly-forward, updateStatus/updateTitleIfNewer monotonic, archiveOrphanedDraft guarded on status).

AutomationStore.insertInvocationGuarded builds one self-guarded batch where the invocation insert is suppressed by INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (overlap predicate), child inserts are 0-row no-ops when the invocation was suppressed, and the schedule advance is a compare-and-set on the exact claimed next_run_at slot; a UNIQUE violation (cron double-fire, event dedup) rolls back the whole batch including the advance, and callers classify via isUniqueConstraintError in db/errors.ts.

Invocation status is never stored: automation_invocations status/completion are derived in SQL (DERIVED_INVOCATION_STATUS_SQL / DERIVED_INVOCATION_COMPLETED_AT_SQL) from child automation_runs, with a TS twin deriveInvocationStatus that integration tests assert agrees with the SQL definition.

automation_runs snapshot their repository and environment targets at firing time (repo_owner/name/id/base_branch, environment_id) so history never depends on the live automation selection, and every run carries a required invocation_id since migration 0059, which copied rows unfiltered so a NULL invocation_id would abort the migration rather than being silently repaired.

session_pull_requests is the D1 authority for PR lifecycle tracking (the DO pr artifact is a live-view mirror), keyed by the DO artifact id, with canonical (repository_external_id, pr_number) and legacy (repo_owner, repo_name, pr_number) unique identity indexes; upserts implement a SQL-side monotonic provider_updated_at guard so an out-of-order webhook cannot regress state, and a draft is only meaningful while open (CHECK constraint).

Image-build callback completion is accepted atomically: one UPDATE consumes the callback token (provider_session_id, status='building', callback_token_hash, expiry, used_at IS NULL) and distinguishes accepted/replayed/rejected; finalization work is lease-guarded via finalization_lease_token/expires_at columns and dedicated partial indexes for stale recovery.

image_builds is deliberately FK-less so deleting the owning entity supersedes its rows rather than cascading, letting the cleanup reaper still find and delete provider-side artifacts; repo_images was dropped (0040) because its rows are cache entries whose selection fingerprint cannot be computed in SQL.

The ImageBuildStore projects status reads through STATUS_VIEW_KEYS so internal columns (callback tokens, provider session/image ids) never reach a client; the satisfies and exhaustiveness assertions make a leaking column a compile error.

R2 (MEDIA_BUCKET) backs the ObjectStorage port (put/delete/head/get with range support) for chat attachments, screenshots (10 MiB, 100/session), and videos (100 MiB, 20/session); attachment persistence registers the record in the DO first, then puts the object, so every failed or ambiguous storage outcome remains discoverable through the stale-attachment cleanup protocol (register, claim, delete, acknowledge/release, converging in at most 3 attempts).

Attachment records live in the DO's attachments table (with cleanup_claimed_at) while bytes live in R2; attach/release semantics preserve ownership across fallible object deletion via a claim/acknowledge protocol.

KV REPOS_CACHE stores the enriched repository listing (repos:list:v2) with stale-while-revalidate: fresh (< 5 min) serves immediately, stale (5 min to 1 h TTL) serves immediately and refreshes via executionCtx.submit, and a cache miss fetches synchronously while also registering the refresh with waitUntil so the KV write outlives the response; metadata updates delete the key best-effort.

GitHub App installation tokens are cached in memory plus KV (github:installation-token:v1:<appId>:<installationId>) with INSTALLATION_TOKEN_CACHE_MAX_AGE_MS = 50 min, TTL bounded by remaining token lifetime, in-flight refresh deduplication, and non-fatal cache failures; the same REPOS_CACHE namespace is passed as the cache store to the SCM provider.

Better Auth persistence runs through CanonicalSqlAdapter over the SqlDatabase seam directly against canonical tables (users, user_identities) with epoch-ms timestamps, INTEGER booleans, caller-generated ids, and transactions: false because D1 exposes no interactive transactions — register self-heals at the next sign-in through implicit linking and the claim decorator.

Migration 0057 is the hard identity cutover: it folds the Better Auth registry (auth_users/auth_accounts) into the canonical registry (users/user_identities), requires an operator preflight with a D1 Time Travel bookmark as rollback and count checks, never deletes identity data, and adds email_verified as the implicit-linking gate.
Automation trigger_auth_data is dual-purpose: a SHA-256 hash for webhook automations and AES-256-GCM ciphertext for sentry automations (renamed from webhook_secret_hash by migration 0016).

D1 index architecture for automations has been corrected over time for query shape: partial indexes must match sweep queries by bare equality (idx_runs_orphan_sweep status='starting', idx_runs_timeout_sweep status='running', idx_runs_active_lookup status IN ('starting','running')) because a non-matching predicate silently full-scans the append-only automation_runs table.

The session inbox is computed by recursive CTEs over the D1 sessions table (eligible_sessions, rerooted_sessions, effective_sessions, inbox_roots) that re-root filtered subtrees while retaining the persisted root_session_id, categorize by unread/active/finished, and page by root with a cursor; eligibility excludes archived sessions and optionally automation-generated lineage.

Sessions analytics (AnalyticsStore) aggregates over the D1 sessions table grouped by status/spawn_source with COALESCE(user_id, scm_login) for active-user counting, and PR analytics range-scans COALESCE(provider_created_at, created_at) and merged_at, backed by the expression and partial indexes from migration 0042.

Managed skills are content-addressed: skills point at immutable skill_revisions (revision_sha256, unique skill+revision_number) with revision files, checked scope assignments, a catalog generation counter, and per-session pinned manifests snapshotted atomically at session create (or copied from the parent for agent-spawned children); skill_import_sources records repo-import provenance that survives later hand edits.

Model-provider account credentials are stored encrypted with associated-data binding and guarded by CAS columns (credential_version, exchange_generation, exchange_state with in_flight owner, lifecycle_version), and device-flow authorizations carry state/lifecycle CHECKs tying processing rows to an owner, giving atomicity for create/reconnect exchanges over non-transactional D1.

Migration style reflects D1 constraints: large data transforms use guarded idempotent backfills (0030, 0057), table rebuilds are staged because SQLite cannot drop CHECK-referenced columns under enforced FKs and D1 forbids PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF mid-transaction (0029, 0031 stage children, drop them to release FK claims, rebuild the parent, and recreate children), and wrangler's migration splitter treats a bare END as a terminator (IIF used instead of CASE in 0030).

UserScmTokenStore and the session participant repository store SCM credentials encrypted under TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY; the D1 user_scm_tokens row's raw refresh-token ciphertext is used as the CAS comparand during rotation, and participants.ws_auth_token stores only a SHA-256 hash of the WebSocket auth token.
